hook: SCP-604 is a set of jeweled plates and goblets that turn whatever food is served on them into human flesh, and turn living animals into moving human body parts. It is one of the most graphic Safe-class files you can pick up: cannibalism, infant body parts, mutilated animals and a severed head that is aware of what is about to happen are all described directly. If you go in, the real subject turns out to be the people who wanted to eat from it.
whyItMatters:
The article is a sharp portrait of Marshall, Carter and Dark, the group that acquired the set and ran it as a luxury dining attraction. The anomaly is horrible, but the supporting documents make it clear that the worst parts come from the business built around it.

It also shows how flat, procedural language can make atrocity land harder. The cooks discuss garnish choices and the guests trade jokes, and the file records it all with the same neutral detail as the property list.
thingsToNotice:
The description works like a menu of rules, explaining how a steak becomes a thigh cut, why small plates mostly produce infant parts, and how garnishes survive the change. The origin story then adds a religious layer: an abbey used the set for communion, experiencing visions of a loving God while eating what the priests called the body of Jesus, a reaction the Foundation could not reproduce.

The logs are ordered as escalation. Diners complain that the result tastes like pork, cooks treat failed cakes and slug sculptures as kitchen experiments, a snake becomes a screaming throat, and a pile of leeches yields a head buried under them that shrieks for help. The last log answers the question the clients were paying for: a mewling animal kept on IV lines inside a box becomes a fully conscious man's head, confused about who he is, and the waiter simply wishes the guests a good meal as he starts to scream.
